rounds.text: Telge Projects Ltd demonstrates exceptional compounding capability, evidenced by a 3-year compounded sales growth of 40% [E8] and a matching 3-year profit growth of 39% [E10]. This top-line momentum is further reinforced by recent performance, with quarterly sales showing a 53% year-on-year surge and net profit expanding by 47% to 48% year-on-year [E41, E43, E48]. The underlying profitability is backed by a strong historical return profile, highlighted by a 3-year median return on equity of 24% [E13] and an overall good ROE track record [E36]. Balance sheet stewardship remains prudent, demonstrated by a conservative debt-to-equity ratio of 0.26x alongside a reduction in total borrowings [E23, E24, E35]. Moreover, promoter confidence is rising as insider holdings increased by 0.51 percentage points to reach 72.16% [E26], aligning with a major operational inflection where quarterly operating margins rebounded by 7 percentage points year-on-year to 24% [E16]. conceded: [E19], [E38].

Telge Projects Ltd trades at an expensive P/E of 56.1 and a price-to-book ratio of 4.28x, leaving the stock vulnerable to a valuation correction [E1, E2]. This rich pricing is hard to justify given that the DCF model places intrinsic value at ₹ 116 per share compared to the market price of ₹ 161, resulting in a negative margin of safety of -38.6% [E30, E31]. Furthermore, the reverse DCF indicates that today's market price demands an aggressive 22.4% earnings growth, surpassing the base case assumption of 18.0% [E32]. Operational efficiency is also deteriorating, marked by high debtors of 153 days and working capital days stretching from 112 to 159 days [E38, E39]. This cash flow strain is evident in the negative operating cash flow of ₹ -3.49 Cr and negative free cash flow of ₹ -5.83 Cr for Mar 2026, leading to a poor cash conversion ratio of -1.44x [E19, E20, E21]. Compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months has dropped to -23%, while operating margins have compressed by 8 percentage points over three years [E11, E15]. Institutional confidence is fading as well, reflected by negative money flow with foreign and domestic institutions cutting their holdings by a combined 2.51 percentage points [E27, E28, E29]. Conceded: the company demonstrates healthy 3-year compounded sales growth of 40% and a low debt-to-equity ratio of 0.26x [E8, E23].

Conceded: [E1], [E2], [E30], [E31], [E32], [E27], [E28], and [E29]. While the bear focuses on rich valuation multiples and institutional outflows, it ignores the exceptional multi-year fundamental growth that underpins the stock's price, including a 40% compounded sales growth and 39% compounded profit growth over three years [E8, E10]. Conceded: [E19], [E20], [E21], [E38], and [E39]. However, pointing out short-term cash flow strains overlooks the impressive recent operational inflection where quarterly operating margins rebounded by 7 percentage points year-over-year in June 2026, alongside robust top-line momentum with sales and net profit surging over 45% YoY [E16, E41, E43]. Conceded: [E11] and [E15]. Yet, relying on trailing numbers completely misses the ongoing turnaround where results score a perfect 100/100 and accelerate strongly, proving that the business is actively outperforming a broader construction sector that sits at sluggish single-digit growth rates [E48, E51].

Conceded: [E8], [E10], [E16], [E41], [E43], [E48], and [E51]. While multi-year growth figures and recent quarterly margin expansions exist, they distract from the severe deterioration in trailing-twelve-month profit growth which stands at -23% and an operating margin contraction of 8 percentage points over a three-year span [E11, E15]. Pointing to an accelerating quarterly turnaround does not erase the severe working capital bottleneck where debtors have ballooned to 153 days and working capital days have surged from 112 to 159 days [E38, E39]. This cash trap is directly evidenced by negative operating cash flow of Rs -3.49 Cr and free cash flow of Rs -5.83 Cr in March 2026, meaning reported profits are entirely disconnected from actual cash generation [E20, E21]. Furthermore, dismissing valuation and institutional behavior as irrelevant ignores a discounted cash flow intrinsic value of Rs 116 against a market price of Rs 161, leaving a -38.6% margin of safety alongside a heavy institutional money outflow of 2.68 percentage points [E29, E30, E31].
